punchline: Gibson says healing starts with a goal of your own for each conversation, and not with a parent who finally changes.
thirty_sec: Lindsay Gibson calls it the healing fantasy: adult children keep believing the parent will eventually change and give them the love and validation they missed. Her first step points elsewhere, to your own authentic self and true feelings. Then she suggests relating to the parent instead of being embedded in the relationship, and entering each interaction with a clear goal. To practice, you replay a bad conversation and name the goal you could have brought.
